cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul goes there on foot. His friends take the ship, and Paul takes his own two feet. Verse 13 says he arranged it that way because he was going there on foot. Then he meets them at Assos and they take him aboard (Acts 20:14). I think that's a man who knew exactly where he'd be standing when the boat pulled in.

The answer is to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost. Verse 16 says Paul was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost. That's why he decided to sail past Ephesus, since he didn't want to spend time in the province of Asia. I'd say that's a man watching the calendar, friends.

The answer is the elders of the church. From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church. He's sailing past Ephesus, so he has them come to him. Funny how a man in a hurry still makes time for the people who matter.

The answer is publicly and from house to house. Paul says he taught the Ephesians that way, and that covers the big gatherings and the living rooms. He also says he did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to them.

The answer is repentance to God and faith in Jesus. Verse 21 says Paul was testifying “…about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.” That's the heart of what he told them. Turn to God, trust Jesus.

The answer is True. Paul says he was “…testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.” The word is alike, so the same message went to both. Nobody got a different version.
The answer is True. Paul says, “…in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.” That's a lot of warnings. And he keeps heading toward Jerusalem anyway.

The answer is finishing the ministry Jesus gave him. Paul says he considers his life of no value to himself, “…if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus…” That ministry is testifying to the good news of God's grace. With chains ahead, that's still the thing he wants most.

The answer is False. Paul says, “Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.” No return visit is promised. That sets up the tears at the end of this passage.

The answer is shepherds. Paul says, “Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.” A flock needs someone who guards it and keeps it together. That's the job he hands these elders.

The answer is wolves. Paul says, “I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.” Wolves are the natural enemy of a flock, so he keeps his picture together. It's a warning, and he wants them awake for it.

The answer is that they will distort the truth to draw disciples after them. Paul says those men will “…distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.” They twist the truth and gather followers for themselves. That's why he wants the elders alert.

The answer is that they can be built up and given an inheritance. Paul says the word of His grace “…can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.” So the word does the building. And the inheritance is shared with all who are sanctified.

The answer is hands. Paul says, “…these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.” He worked to provide for himself and his friends. I know a little about working with hands, though mine is a mustache.
The answer is “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” Paul remembers those words of the Lord Jesus, and he says it's by hard work like his that we must help the weak. Giving is the point.
The answer is that he prays with them. Verse 36 says Paul knelt down with all of them and prayed. After a long goodbye talk, he ends on his knees with them. No speeches this time.
The answer is False. The text says, “They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.” Nobody held anything back. I think this was a hard goodbye.
The answer is to the ship. Verse 38 says they accompanied him to the ship. They'd prayed and wept together, and they still went with him there. I think nobody wanted to be the first to turn around.
